title: Cyprus's Akrotiri Peninsula: Ophiolite Island, Seasonal Lake, Flamingo Decline
content:
NASA Earth Observatory recently published a feature detailing the geological and biological history of Cyprus, centered on imagery captured by the Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager on October 10, 2026. The images focus on the Akrotiri Peninsula, the southernmost tip of the island, where seasonal rains had begun to fill the Akrotiri Salt Lake. The article explains that Cyprus began forming approximately 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period, when molten rock from the seafloor solidified to create new oceanic crust. Tectonic forces later uplifted portions of this rock, forming a rugged island composed of ophiolite, a green, mottled stone often compared to snake skin. Remnants of this ancient formation are visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains.

During the Miocene, younger layers of chalk, limestone, and other marine sediments accumulated around the original island. These materials eventually formed a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift. Sediments from rivers and marine sources combined to create deltas and two land bridges, known as tombolos, which joined the landmasses into the current Akrotiri Peninsula. The westerly Kouris River tombolo formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from the main island, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea to form the coastal lagoon only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists.

The Akrotiri Salt Lake, situated between the two tombolos, experiences significant seasonal water level changes, typically filling in late autumn and winter before drying out in summer. Historically, the influx of winter water attracted large populations of overwintering flamingos, averaging about 4,000 birds. The flamingos feed on fairy shrimp, which contain carotenoids responsible for the birds’ pink coloration. However, news reports indicate that the wintering flamingo population has declined sharply in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025.

The article also highlights the island’s reputation for snakes and cats. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa, or “land of snakes,” likely due to a robust population of blunt-nosed vipers. Legend states that during a fourth-century drought, Roman Empress Helena ordered shiploads of cats from Egypt to control the venomous reptiles. These cats were first released in the southeastern part of the Akrotiri Peninsula, an area known as Cape Gata, or Cape Cat in Greek. Today, the Holy Monastery of St. Nicholas of the Cats remains in this area, where a handful of nuns care for hundreds of cats.

Current statistics indicate that Cyprus has as many cats as people, with more than one million felines on the island. The NASA Earth Observatory story, written by Adam Voiland and featuring images by Michala Garrison, uses this combination of geological history and wildlife dynamics to illustrate the unique environmental characteristics of the Akrotiri Peninsula.
summary: Cyprus's Akrotiri Peninsula: Ophiolite Island, Seasonal Lake, Flamingo Decline.
author: NASA News

title: UK law to ban simulated incest and some oral sex depictions draws censorship concerns
content: A new United Kingdom law slated to take effect will prohibit simulated incest and certain depictions of oral sex. Adult content creators and free‑speech advocates have voiced alarm about the measure, warning it could represent an unprecedented level of sex censorship.
summary: A new United Kingdom law that will take effect soon bans simulated incest and certain depictions of oral sex. Adult content creators and free‑speech advocates are raising concerns about the ban.
author: Wired

title: Nintendo designers aimed for elegance in Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake
content:
Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake for the Switch 2 blends the classic N64 experience with contemporary visuals and gameplay, preserving the original’s core while adding modern graphics.  

The project is led by producers Eiji Aonuma—former director of the original game and current steward of the franchise at Nintendo—and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, best known for directing Breath of the Wild and its sequel.  The team also includes a number of younger developers, some of whom had never played the original title.
summary: The Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2 smashes together the past and present. The game retains much of the original N64 experience while updating it with modern graphics and gameplay that make it feel contemporary.
author: The Verge

title: Silicon Valley billionaires pictured with Trump face scrutiny from Democratic Congress
content: Democrats’ success was helped by popular anger over tech, AI and the super rich – life for billionaires could become much more difficult The photo of Silicon Valley centi-billionaires at Donald Trump’s inauguration – Musk, Bezos, and Zuckerberg, front row and side by side – now looks like a hitlist for a blue Congress hellbent on making life difficult for billionaires. The picture symbolized at the time the bending of the knee by the richest men in the world to its most powerful, a symbiosis of the ultra-rich. Already unfathomably wealthy, Silicon Valley tycoons believed a Maga-sized public shift to the right would enrich them even more. It did. For several years, while Trump seemed an everlasting kingmaker and AI’s expansion seemed unstoppable, their fortunes ballooned to values beyond comprehension. Elon Musk’s surpassed $1tn.
summary: Silicon Valley billionaires pictured with Trump face scrutiny from Democratic Congress.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Germany pledges €20 million for education in emergencies as crises affect 258 million children
content: In an exclusive Euronews op‑ed, Germany’s Minister for Development Reem Alabali Radovan notes that crises are disrupting the education of 258 million school‑aged children worldwide. In response, Germany will allocate €20 million for education in emergencies over the coming years.
summary: Reem Alabali Radovan, Germany's Minister for Development, says the education of 258 million school‑aged children worldwide is disrupted by crises. Germany will provide €20 million in funding for education in emergencies over the coming years.
author: Euronews

title: Democrats seize US Congress as hackers target French blood bank and supermarkets
content: Democrats have seized control of the U.S. Congress, described as a nationwide rejection of Trump. In Europe, hackers have targeted a French blood bank and supermarket refrigerators, prompting concerns about a new front in hybrid warfare. The program also includes a conversation with Reza Pahlavi, identified as a leading figure in the opposition to the Tehran regime.
summary: Democrats have seized control of the US Congress in a nationwide rejection of Trump. In Europe, hackers targeted a French blood bank and supermarket fridges, raising fears of a new hybrid‑warfare front and featuring a conversation with opposition figure Reza Pahlavi.
author: Euronews

title: CERN scientists find evidence of ultra-rare particle decay at LHC
content: CERN scientists have reported evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay observed with the Large Hadron Collider. The decay, predicted to happen only once in every 10 billion cases, provides researchers with a new avenue for probing the subatomic world.
summary: Scientists at CERN have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay using the Large Hadron Collider. The process is predicted to occur just once in every 10 billion cases, offering researchers a new way to explore the subatomic world.
author: Euronews

title: Volunteer rescuers aid pilot whales in mass stranding on Wairarapa coast, many dead
content: Volunteers in New Zealand are confronting a mass stranding of pilot whales along the Wairarapa coast near Cape Palliser. While they have managed to return at least 14 whales to the sea, many others have been found dead along the remote shoreline. The effort highlights the ongoing challenge of rescuing the stranded cetaceans.
summary: Volunteers in New Zealand are working to save pilot whales stranded along the Wairarapa coast near Cape Palliser. At least 14 have been helped back into the water, but many others have died along the remote coastline.
author: Euronews

title: Displaced Palestinian builds makeshift wind turbine to power tents in Khan Younis
content: A displaced Palestinian in Gaza has constructed a makeshift wind turbine to supply electricity to tents in Khan Younis. Lacking the funds for solar panels, he is using wind power to run everyday essentials for his community.
summary: A displaced Palestinian in Gaza built a makeshift wind turbine to bring electricity to tents in Khan Younis. He did so because he could not afford solar panels and wanted to harness wind for everyday essentials.
author: Euronews

title: Three NASA astronauts vote in U.S. midterm elections from the ISS
content: In a rare occurrence, three American astronauts cast votes in Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station. They used advanced links to transmit electronic ballots to election officials on Earth.
summary: In a rare event, three American astronauts voted in Tuesday's US midterm elections from the International Space Station, using advanced links to send electronic ballots to officials on Earth.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea to deploy military mission to keep Strait of Hormuz open
content: South Korea’s defence ministry announced on Thursday that it will deploy maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive‑ordnance‑disposal team near the Strait of Hormuz to help keep the waterway open. Seoul said the deployment aims to protect commercial shipping and energy supplies, while explicitly ruling out any military intervention in the ongoing US‑Iran war.
summary: South Korea will deploy maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive ordnance disposal team near the Strait of Hormuz to help keep the waterway open, its defence ministry said Thursday. Seoul said it would protect commercial shipping and energy supplies while ruling out military intervention in the ongoing US-Iran war.
author: France 24

title: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years in prison for foreign collusion
content: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 30, was sentenced on Thursday to an additional ten years in prison for colluding with foreign powers, according to a court summary. The sentence follows his September guilty plea to seeking foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing’s national security law, after he had already served nearly six years in custody.
summary: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced on Thursday to an additional 10 years in prison for colluding with foreign powers. He had pleaded guilty in September to seeking foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing’s national security law after spending nearly six years in prison.
author: France 24

title: Melania Trump to host Ukrainian and Russian officials at White House before Abu Dhabi talks
content: Russian and Ukrainian officials, including human‑rights chiefs, are scheduled to meet U.S. First Lady Melania Trump at the White House on Thursday, a gathering set ahead of Abu Dhabi talks aimed at ending the Ukraine war. Weeks earlier, Melania Trump helped broker a partial cease‑fire that enabled civilians to evacuate from the Russian‑occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky.
summary: Russian and Ukrainian officials, including human‑rights chiefs, will meet US First Lady Melania Trump at the White House on Thursday. The meeting precedes Abu Dhabi talks on ending the Ukraine war and follows her role in brokering a partial ceasefire that allowed civilians to leave the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky.
author: France 24

title: France prepares for Thursday nationwide strikes challenging Macron's policies
content: France is preparing for nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Thursday, with trade unions calling on the government to aid households coping with rising living costs. The planned protests follow weeks of social unrest, and the liveblog will provide ongoing updates as the events unfold.
summary: Strikes and demonstrations are scheduled across France on Thursday as trade unions call on the government to aid households facing rising living costs. The protests come after weeks of social unrest.

title: RC Lens lose 9-1 to Como, worst European defeat in French football history
content: RC Lens endured the heaviest defeat in French football history in European competition, losing 9‑1 at home to Como in the Champions League. The loss follows earlier European setbacks, a 3‑0 defeat to Club Brugge and a 2‑0 loss to Sporting CP, marking three consecutive defeats for Lens in Europe.
summary: RC Lens lost 9-1 at home to Como in the Champions League, marking the heaviest defeat for a French club in European competition. The loss followed defeats by Club Brugge (3-0) and Sporting CP (2-0), giving Lens three straight European defeats.
author: France 24

title: Bomb threat forces Dublin‑Rome flight to divert to France
content: An airliner traveling from Dublin to Rome was diverted to France on Thursday after a bomb threat, the French government said. The incident is being reported as breaking news, with further details pending.
summary: An airliner traveling from Dublin to Rome was rerouted to France on Thursday after a bomb threat, the French government said. The incident was reported as a breaking news story with more details to come.

content: An Airbus A320 en route to Rome was forced to make an emergency landing in Evreux, France, after the prime minister’s office reported a bomb threat. The diversion marks the latest of several similar incidents reported in recent days.

title: WHO reports one in four adolescents lack daily 60 minutes of activity
content: One in four adolescents worldwide reported not getting at least 60 minutes of physical activity on any day in the previous week, according to new global estimates released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday.
summary: One in four adolescents worldwide reported not getting at least 60 minutes of physical activity on any day in the previous week. The data come from new global estimates released by the World Health Organization on Wednesday.

content: A member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in Syria said on Wednesday that many children born in the country since the war began in 2011 lack legal identity. The commission noted that Syrian nationality is transmitted only through fathers, and many of those fathers are dead or missing, leaving the children undocumented.
summary: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers. A member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said this on Wednesday.

title: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
content: A war‑induced shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz in February caused oil prices to rise globally. A new UNCTAD report notes that the resulting fuel‑price shock has affected countries unevenly, with developing economies bearing the greatest burden at the pump.
summary: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.

content: On Tuesday, gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region, causing injuries and prompting a humanitarian partner to leave, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said. The incident occurs while aid teams are preparing for winter storms.

content: The United Nations’ peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the pull‑out of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara could create a dangerous security vacuum. He noted that the Security Council remains divided on whether, or how, to replace the departing forces.
summary: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of Blue Helmets from Lebanon and Western Sahara could create a dangerous security vacuum. The Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

content: The summit’s focus, according to the briefing, is that while the world now possesses more tools than ever to address climate change, millions still cannot access them. With clean‑energy technologies progressing rapidly, the key challenge for countries at COP31 is ensuring those solutions are affordable for everyone.

title: Aer Lingus Dublin‑Rome flight diverted to Evreux military base after bomb threat
content: France’s prime minister’s office confirmed that an Aer Lingus flight operating from Dublin to Rome was redirected to a military base in Évreux after a bomb threat. Flight‑tracking data from Flightradar24 indicated that the aircraft followed its normal route across the English Channel, then turned south‑west of Paris, looped around Chartres Airport and headed toward Évreux. The tracker also noted that no aircraft had taken off from Rome’s Fiumicino Airport in the preceding 30 minutes.
summary: Aer Lingus Dublin‑Rome flight diverted to Evreux military base after bomb threat.

title: Italian chef Davide Tamburella loses bid to regain job after pineapple pizza refusal
content:
Australia’s Fair Work Commission heard that chef Davide Tamburella was dismissed after he refused to use pineapple as a pizza topping, a decision he later challenged but was unable to overturn.  

The dispute involved La Costa, a restaurant in Queensland that was presented as an “elegant slice of Italy” with sea‑foam‑green and white décor, exposed brick columns, classic Italian dishes served on European oak tables and a website promise of an Italian Riviera experience. The venue has since closed.
summary: Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the Queensland restaurant La Costa after refusing to put pineapple on pizza. The Fair Work Commission heard his case and ruled that his bid to be reinstated was unsuccessful.

title: Pauline Hanson to appeal high court racial discrimination ruling over Pakistan comment
content:
Australia’s High Court has agreed to hear Pauline Hanson’s appeal against a 2024 ruling that she engaged in racial discrimination against Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi. The appeal follows a unanimous decision by the full federal court earlier this year, which upheld the original ruling and found that Hanson’s remarks—told to “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”—portrayed Faruqi as a “second‑class citizen”.

The One Nation leader was granted special leave to appeal on Thursday. The High Court’s acceptance of the appeal marks the next stage in the legal proceedings over Hanson’s comments toward the senator.
summary: Pauline Hanson to appeal high court racial discrimination ruling over Pakistan comment.

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon testifies he accessed Jesse Baird’s phone, poured water in fuel tank
content: Beau Lamarre‑Condon, the accused double murderer, testified in a double‑murder trial that he examined Jesse Baird’s phone and poured water into Baird’s fuel tank. The court adjourned for lunch, with Lamarre‑Condon scheduled to resume his evidence at 2 p.m., while members of the public gathered to watch his testimony.
summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon testifies he accessed Jesse Baird’s phone, poured water in fuel tank.

title: South Korea to seek parliament vote to extend Cheonghae unit 650km from Strait of Hormuz
content:
South Korea’s defence ministry announced plans to expand the operational area of its anti-piracy Cheonghae unit to waters near the port of Duqm in Oman, approximately 650 kilometers from the strait of Hormuz. This move follows criticism from Donald Trump regarding South Korea’s support for his war in Iran. The government intends to submit a motion to parliament to authorize this extended area of operation.

The proposed expansion requires approval from both the national assembly and President Lee Jae Myung, along with the cabinet. By shifting the Cheonghae unit’s focus closer to the vital maritime chokepoint, Seoul is responding to direct pressure from the United States to provide greater support in the region.
summary: South Korea will seek parliamentary approval to expand the Cheonghae anti‑piracy unit’s operational area to waters near Duqm, Oman, about 650 km from the Strait of Hormuz. The motion also requires approval by President Lee Jae Myung and the cabinet after criticism from Donald Trump over South Korea’s support for the Iran war.
author: Guardian World

title: UK MPs say country dangerously dependent on China for defence and AI critical minerals
content: Delivering net zero also at risk, say MPs as they call for centralised policy and funding for mines and diversification The UK is “dangerously” dependent on China for critical raw materials needed for the military, renewable energy infrastructure and AI, a parliamentary investigation has found. MPs on the business select committee called for an urgent centralised policy and the creation of a “critical minerals finance facility” to help fund rare earth and other critical mineral mines, and deploy grants, equity and debt to accelerate a diversification programme.
summary: UK MPs say country dangerously dependent on China for defence and AI critical minerals.
author: Guardian World

title: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in Hong Kong national security case
content: Wong, 30, in prison since 2020, is only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law Exclusive: Joshua Wong laments city’s fate from inside maximum security prison The Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after earlier pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city. Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations, submitted his guilty plea in September. He had been accused of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China.
summary: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in Hong Kong national security case.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump Proclaims American Space Superiority in Election Night Declaration
content:
On November 3, President Trump issued the "American Declaration of Freedom in Space," a proclamation asserting that space is the "province of all humans" open for exploration. The document declares the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system under United States laws, positioning the U.S. as the leader of humanity’s expansion into the cosmos. While the proclamation invokes the nation’s "frontier spirit" and cites Apollo 11 astronauts and robotic Mars rovers as examples of American leadership, it does not introduce new funding, programs, or policy directives.

The declaration emphasizes the administration’s goals for NASA’s Artemis program, which aims to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually send them to Mars. It highlights the success of the Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon, setting a record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. According to the proclamation, the follow-up Artemis III mission is scheduled to launch in the summer of 2027 to test rendezvous and docking operations between the Orion spacecraft and commercial lunar landers. Artemis IV is targeted for 2028 as the program’s first lunar landing mission, with a December 2025 executive order reaffirming the goal of deploying initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030.

The document pledges that the United States will carry values of faith, freedom, and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization, stating that "American space superiority for all eternity" will be ensured by the country’s flourishing commercial space sector. Although the proclamation does not establish new NASA programs or allocate additional funding, its language echoes principles from the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.
summary: President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws.
author: Space.com

title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
content:
On November 4, 2015, the United States Air Force attempted a debut launch of the experimental Super Strypi rocket from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The rail-launched vehicle was designed to carry small payloads into orbit, marking a modern evolution of the 1960s Strypi sounding rocket. The mission intended to place 13 tiny satellites, known as cubesats, into space, but the launch failed less than a minute after liftoff.

The rocket lifted off at approximately 9:45 p.m. local time on November 3, 2015, but quickly spun out of control and crashed. The failure likely resulted from a problem with the first-stage motor and destroyed all 13 cubesats aboard. The primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, also nicknamed HiakaSat, which was built by engineers at the University of Hawaii for the Air Force to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment. The remaining 12 payloads included eight cubesats for NASA’s Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission and four additional university payloads.

Super Strypi was a three-stage rocket powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, designed to reach orbit rather than suborbital trajectories. The Air Force hoped the system would serve as a tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs, capable of launching up to 300 kilograms of payload for $15 million per mission. Following the 2015 failure, the program never recovered, and the Air Force did not attempt another launch with this rocket.

In the years since the failure, the U.S. Space Force has shifted its strategy for fast-turnaround launch support to commercial companies. In June of this year, the Space Force partnered with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with only 17 hours of notice, setting a new record for short-turnaround launch response.
summary: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii.
author: Space.com

title: Bournemouth's calm approach after Marco Rose's winless start is paying off
content:
Bournemouth’s decision to remain calm following a difficult start to the Premier League season is beginning to pay off. The club’s head coach, Marco Rose, failed to secure a victory in his first six league matches, recording three defeats and three draws. This initial lack of success, combined with the summer departure of his predecessor, Andoni Iraola, led to media speculation regarding Rose’s future and concern among supporters.

However, the club maintained a positive and steady approach, recognizing that new tactical methods often require time to produce results. Bournemouth fans drew parallels to Iraola’s tenure, noting that he also did not win any of his first nine Premier League games upon taking charge. Despite that slow start, Iraola ultimately made a significant impact on the team, a precedent that supports the current patience shown toward Rose.
summary: Bournemouth did not win any of their first six Premier League games under new head coach Marco Rose, but the club remained calm and positive. Fans recalled that previous coach Andoni Iraola also lost his first nine matches before making a significant impact.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wilder to face Opetaia on Fury v Joshua undercard in Cardiff
content:
Deontay Wilder, the 41-year-old former World Boxing Council heavyweight champion, will fight unbeaten Australian cruiserweight world champion Jai Opetaia on the undercard of the Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua bout in Cardiff on 11 December. Organizers announced the matchup on Wednesday, noting that Opetaia will move up in weight to face one of history’s most devastating punchers at the Principality Stadium.

Wilder has won 43 of his 45 victories by knockout. The event will stream live worldwide on Netflix.
summary: Former World Boxing Council heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder will face unbeaten Australian cruiserweight world champion Jai Opetaia on 11 December. The fight will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff and stream live worldwide on Netflix.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ravens near trade with Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett amid QB injury crisis
content:
Veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett is set to move from the Arizona Cardinals to the Baltimore Ravens, according to a source with knowledge of the deal who spoke to the Associated Press on Wednesday. The individual requested anonymity because the transaction has not yet been finalized. The trade emerges as the Ravens navigate a significant injury crisis at the quarterback position.

Baltimore’s starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, is out indefinitely due to an injured thumb. Additionally, backup quarterback Huntley will miss the remainder of the season with a turf toe injury. Consequently, rookie Fagnano is scheduled to start for the Ravens in Thursday’s game.
summary: Ravens near trade with Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett amid QB injury crisis.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Erling Haaland settles thriller for Manchester City to end RB Leipzig resistance
content: Erling Haaland scored the winning goal for Manchester City against RB Leipzig, ending the German side’s resistance. The forward slid home a cross from Elliot Anderson to secure the victory for Enzo Maresca’s team. Rayan Cherki also hit the post late in the match.
summary: Feed Erling Haaland and Manchester City’s totemic No 9 will score. The problem, recently, has been a paucity of openings for him.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Viktor Gyökeres leads Arsenal to nervy win against Slavia Prague
content:
Arsenal secured a narrow victory against Slavia Prague in a European away fixture, with Viktor Gyökeres highlighted as the decisive performer. The Czech champions extended their winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history to 23 matches, equalling the record held by AEK Athens and FCSB. Despite this, Slavia Prague mounted a spirited late comeback that tested Arsenal’s defense.

The match remained tense until the end, as Wiktor Nowak pulled one back for Slavia Prague. However, a crucial save by David Raya prevented the Czech side from earning a point, preserving Arsenal’s win. This result maintains Arsenal’s unbeaten record in their last 10 away trips, though manager Mikel Arteta’s team displayed defensive vulnerabilities under pressure.
summary: Viktor Gyökeres scored as Arsenal defeated Slavia Prague, a result that left the Czech team with a 23-match winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history. Arsenal maintained their unbeaten record in their last 10 away trips despite a late goal from Wiktor Nowak and a crucial save by David Raya.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Valverde late goal earns Real Madrid win at AEK Athens
content: Real Madrid maintained their perfect Champions League record with a late victory against AEK Athens, secured by a goal from captain Federico Valverde. The result marked AEK's third consecutive defeat in the competition.
summary: Real Madrid secured a late victory against AEK Athens through a goal from captain Federico Valverde. The win extends Real Madrid's 100% start to their Champions League campaign while marking AEK Athens' third consecutive loss.
author: BBC Sport

title: Como Set Champions League Record With 9-1 Away Win Over Lens
content: Anastasios Douvikas scored a hat-trick as Como secured a 9-1 away victory over Lens on match day four. This result stands as the biggest away win in Champions League history.
summary: Anastasios Douvikas scored a hat-trick as Como defeated Lens 9-1 in a Champions League match. This result stands as the biggest away win in Champions League history.

title: Liverpool lose to Fenerbahce in Champions League
content: Liverpool suffered a defeat at the hands of Turkish side Fenerbahce, a result that ended the Reds' perfect start to this year's Champions League after four games. Fenerbahce secured a famous victory by twice fighting back from behind to overcome Liverpool.
summary: Liverpool were defeated by Turkish side Fenerbahce, who twice fought back from behind to seal a victory. This result ended the Reds' perfect start to the Champions League after four games.

content: A world record of 43 players and eight members of staff were sent off during an under-20 championship match between Uberlandia and Mamore in Brazil.
summary: A total of 43 players and eight staff members were sent off during an under-20 championship match in Brazil. The incident occurred in a game between Uberlandia and Mamore, setting a new world record.

title: Arsenal beat Slavia Prague in Champions League, third win from four
content: Arsenal secured their third victory in four Champions League matches against Slavia Prague. Goals from Noni Madueke and Victor Gyokeres proved decisive, although the hosts mounted a valiant late effort to return to the contest.

title: Haaland scores winner as Man City beat Leipzig 3-2 in Champions League
content: Erling Haaland scored the decisive goal as Manchester City defeated RB Leipzig 3‑2 on match day four of the UEFA Champions League group phase, overcoming two instances of being pegged back during the game.

title: Liverpool Lose to Fenerbahce as Dirk Kuyt Celebrates 'Miracle' in Istanbul
content: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola described his team’s defeat by Fenerbahce in Istanbul as resulting from "cheap" and "messy" goals. Former Liverpool player Dirk Kuyt celebrated the result, referring to it as a "miracle" in Istanbul.

title: Texas state rep calls on Abbott to curb Hinojosa’s power before inauguration
content: Texas State Rep. Brian Harrison (R) urged Governor Greg Abbott (R) to limit the future authority of Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) prior to her inauguration next year. Harrison argued that Republicans currently hold “total power in Texas” and must utilize the remaining ten weeks to restore separation of powers and limit Hinojosa’s influence.
summary: Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison (R) on Wednesday called on Gov.

title: Democrat Annie Andrews wins South Carolina race against Darline Graham
content: NPR's Ailsa Chang spoke with Democrat Dr. Annie Andrews, the South Carolina election winner. Andrews defeated Republican incumbent Darline Graham, who is the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.
summary: Democrat Dr. Annie Andrews defeated Republican candidate Darline Graham in a South Carolina election. NPR's Ailsa Chang spoke with Andrews about her victory and the path ahead.
author: NPR Politics

title: VIB and KU Leuven find ASPM mutations disrupt neural stem cells, causing microcephaly
content:
Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven have identified how mutations in the ASPM gene disrupt the development of neural stem cells essential for human brain growth. This disruption causes microcephaly, a condition defined by an abnormally small brain and head, which is frequently accompanied by intellectual disability. The findings, published in Developmental Cell, clarify the specific mechanisms behind this developmental failure.

The study also highlights how variations in brain development render humans more susceptible to certain genetic conditions than other mammals. By uncovering these distinct developmental pathways, the research provides insight into the unique vulnerability of the human brain to ASPM gene mutations.
summary: Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven have uncovered how mutations in the ASPM gene disrupt the development of neural stem cells that help the human brain grow. This disruption explains how these mutations cause microcephaly, a condition characterized by an abnormally small brain and head, often accompanied by intellectual disability.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UCLA team scales CRISPR sickle cell therapy for clinical trial
content: A UCLA-led team has detailed the progression of an experimental CRISPR approach for sickle cell disease into a blood stem cell therapy. The team described how the treatment was advanced to meet the manufacturing scale and quality standards required for a clinical trial.
summary: A UCLA‑led team advanced an experimental CRISPR approach for sickle cell disease into a blood stem cell therapy. The therapy can be manufactured at the scale and quality required for a clinical trial.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Shockwave therapy likely cuts short‑term frozen‑shoulder pain, long‑term benefit unclear
content: A recent review of the latest trial evidence published by The BMJ reports that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduces short‑term pain associated with frozen shoulder. The review also finds that manipulation under anesthesia—whether combined with steroid injections or not—probably improves short‑term flexion compared with usual care.
summary: Extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduces short‑term pain associated with frozen shoulder. Manipulation under anesthesia, with or without steroid injections, probably improves short‑term arm flexion compared with usual care, according to a BMJ review of recent trial evidence.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Unfortified plant-based dairy swaps may cause nutrient deficiencies
content: A new study from the University of Surrey reports that replacing dairy products, even partially, with unfortified plant-based alternatives may lead to deficiencies in vital nutrients. The research suggests that mandatory fortification of these plant-based alternatives and other foods, such as bread, could lessen the risk of such deficiencies, particularly iodine deficiency.
summary: A University of Surrey study reports that replacing dairy with unfortified plant-based alternatives may lead to deficiencies in vital nutrients. The researchers suggest that mandatory fortification of these products and other foods could reduce the risk of such deficiencies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: U.S. experts warn fireworks pose underestimated public health danger
content: U.S. experts warn in The BMJ that fireworks pose an underestimated danger to public health. They recommend implementing stronger regulations and sustained public education campaigns to prevent devastating yet entirely avoidable injuries.
summary: Fireworks pose an underestimated danger to public health and require stronger regulations and sustained public education campaigns to help prevent devastating yet entirely avoidable injuries, warn U. S.

title: Study: Routine breast imaging offers little benefit after double mastectomy for DCIS
content: A new study led by investigators at the UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center suggests that routine breast imaging, such as mammograms, may offer little benefit to women who have undergone a double mastectomy. The research focuses on patients treated for ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), a noninvasive form of breast cancer also known as stage 0 breast cancer.
summary: Study: Routine breast imaging offers little benefit after double mastectomy for DCIS.

title: Stanford study links brain firing patterns to early Alzheimer's prediction
content: New Stanford Medicine-led research indicates that specific brain firing patterns in cognitively normal adults can predict Alzheimer's disease years before memory loss or the accumulation of plaques and tangles. The study also found that distinct firing patterns in other individuals signal unusual resilience to cognitive decline, suggesting a trajectory toward "super ager" status.
summary: New Stanford Medicine-led research found that specific brain firing patterns in cognitively normal adults can predict Alzheimer's disease years before memory loss occurs. Other distinct firing patterns indicated unusual resilience to cognitive decline and a trajectory toward super ager status.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Australian pediatricians lack tools to help teens quit vaping
content: New research from Federation University reveals that two-thirds of Australian pediatricians lack knowledge of where to refer adolescents seeking support to quit vaping. This finding highlights a significant gap in the medical response to youth vaping, indicating that many doctors are unequipped to direct teens toward appropriate cessation resources.
summary: New Federation University research indicates that two-thirds of Australian pediatricians do not know where to refer adolescents for vaping cessation support. This finding highlights a critical gap in the medical response to youth vaping.

title: Bournemouth University Research Finds Iron Age King Verica Was Female
content: Bournemouth University archaeological research indicates that the Iron Age British ruler "Verica" was female. Verica was central to the Roman invasion of Britain in A.D. 43. This discovery rewrites the history of early Roman Britain.
summary: Bournemouth University (BU) archaeological research has revealed that Iron Age British ruler "Verica," who was central to the Roman invasion of Britain in A. D.

title: Scientists reveal how cosignaling receptors dually regulate T cell activation via phase separation
content: Scientists have identified how cosignaling receptors dually regulate T cell activation through phase separation. While prior research established that the T cell receptor (TCR) undergoes phase separation with the kinase Lck to mediate rapid activation upon antigen stimulation, the specific mechanism by which costimulating receptors influence this process had previously remained unclear.
summary: Previous studies showed that the T cell receptor undergoes phase separation with the kinase Lck to mediate rapid T cell activation. The manner in which costimulating receptors regulate this process has remained unclear.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Sydney researchers directly observe hydrogen in metal crystal lattices
content: University of Sydney researchers have directly observed hydrogen dissolved in the minute gaps between atoms within metal alloys. This world-first observation of hydrogen in metal crystal lattices provides new insights into how hydrogen weakens metals and could aid in the development of more hydrogen-resistant materials.
summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney have directly observed hydrogen dissolved in the tiny gaps between atoms in metal alloys. The world‑first observation offers fresh insight into why hydrogen can weaken metals and may help develop more hydrogen‑resistant materials.
author: Phys.org

title: Brazil ranchers on Dirty List bypass forced labor rules via intermediaries
content:
Brazil’s "Dirty List," a public registry identifying employers who violated anti-slavery laws, remains a central tool in the country’s fight against forced labor. Major meatpackers have committed to sustainable sourcing by refusing to buy cattle directly from ranchers named on this list. However, new research indicates that these safeguards are being circumvented. Ranchers on the list are rerouting their cattle through intermediaries, effectively bypassing the direct purchase restrictions.

This practice allows cattle associated with forced labor to continue moving through domestic and international beef and leather supply chains. The findings suggest that the current sourcing commitments are insufficient to prevent the exploitation of workers, as the use of middlemen obscures the origin of the livestock from the meatpackers.
summary: New research indicates that Brazilian ranchers on the anti-slavery Dirty List reroute cattle through intermediaries to avoid direct sales restrictions. This practice allows cattle linked to forced labor to remain in domestic and international beef and leather supply chains.
author: Phys.org

title: European orbiter detects fresh hints of volcanic activity on Mars
content: New data from a European orbiter suggests Mars may still possess internal geological activity. Gas seeping above volcanic rifts in the Alba Mons region indicates that fresh fissures could be allowing gases from the planet’s interior to reach the surface, challenging the notion that Mars is geologically dead.
summary: New evidence from gas seeping above volcanic rifts suggests Mars is not geologically dead but merely sleeping. Fresh fissures along the Alba Mons region hint at active spots where gases from inside the planet may be reaching the surface.
author: Phys.org

title: Earth atmosphere emulators could enable faster and more accurate weather predictions
content: Partitioning the Earth from just below the surface to the top of the atmosphere into 1-kilometer-square chunks results in billions of cells. Running these cells through complex physics equations allows the entire Earth system to interact and evolve in detail, one step at a time.
summary: Dividing the Earth system into 1-kilometer-square chunks requires running billions of cells through complex physics equations. This detailed simulation allows the entire Earth system to interact and evolve step by step.
author: Phys.org

title: New Theoretical Route for Calculating Gluon Production in Proton-Nucleus Collisions
content: Theoretical studies of proton-nucleus collisions describe colliding projectiles as streams of color charges moving along specific trajectories. These charges couple to gluons, which subsequently generate the particles observed in the final state, including gluons and quarks that eventually form hadrons.
summary: Theoretical studies describe colliding projectiles in proton-nucleus collisions as streams of color charges moving along their trajectories. These color charges couple to gluons, which produce the final-state particles observed as gluons, quarks, and hadrons.
author: Phys.org

title: Prehistoric engravings dated at least 19,000 years discovered in Spanish cave
content: A close examination of a frequently visited cave wall in Spain has revealed a spectacular assembly of rock‑art engravings that researchers believe are at least 19,000 years old. The discovery highlights the cave’s significance as a site of prehistoric art.
summary: A frequently visited cave wall in Spain contains a spectacular assembly of rock art engravings. The engravings are thought to be at least 19,000 years old.

title: Gauge open-sources CLI to recursively improve docs for coding agents
content:
Evan from Gauge has announced the open-sourcing of a command-line interface (CLI) designed to recursively improve documentation for coding agents. The tool includes a local execution backend, allowing users to try it without creating an account. An explainer video is available to demonstrate the functionality, and the project is hosted on GitHub with installation instructions provided via npm.

The CLI operates on a "hillclimbing loop" designed to optimize agent-facing surfaces such as documentation, Skills, and CLIs. The process involves setting up tasks for coding agents, running those tasks, and analyzing session transcripts to identify friction or failures. Users then create variants of their documentation to resolve these issues and re-run the tasks with the new variants injected transparently at the same hostname. This cycle repeats until a variant successfully resolves the identified problems.

The system’s architecture consists of two main components: virtual machines and a network gateway. The VMs are designed to be highly privileged to accurately represent developers' coding agents, typically containing the agent harness, language toolchains, and a git repository. The network gateway terminates TLS connections and swaps in documentation variants while handling credential replacement. This ensures that agents see placeholders for credentials and cannot exfiltrate keys. For local execution, the CLI uses Docker containers for VMs and runs mitmproxy in a sidecar container for each session to manage the network gateway.

Gauge stated that they began two years ago building open-source developer tools, including Tach, before pivoting to AI Search optimization and now focusing on the intersection of both fields. The team noted that devtool companies they worked with were the first to ask how to optimize for Claude Code and Codex. The CLI provides primitives for documentation, developer relations, and engineering teams to measure and improve how coding agents utilize their products.

The team has used the hillclimbing loop internally to fix issues such as mistaken pricing, inaccurate product limitations, and repeated workarounds. They identified that coding agents incorrectly reported Gauge only supported Claude Code and Codex, traced this to specific web pages, and corrected the documentation to include support for Pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity. Additionally, Gauge assisted Clerk in shifting coding agents from a legacy "keyless" mode to a new "clerk init" command. After validating a pre-release change to SDK error messages using the tool, Clerk observed a threefold increase in coding agents using the "clerk init" command post-deployment.

The developers argue that the static nature of AI models enables closed-loop optimization for software products, as the same agent can be simulated repeatedly in a high-fidelity testing environment. They emphasize that achieving optimal results requires high-quality analysis to find generalizable friction and paired experiments that vary only the content to measure downstream behavioral changes. The post invites feedback from the Hacker News community on whether this approach improves upon DIY or in-house solutions and what changes might be necessary.
summary: Gauge has open-sourced a CLI that uses a hillclimbing loop to analyze session transcripts and create doc variants to resolve coding agent friction. The tool includes a local execution backend using Docker containers and a network gateway to transparently swap in documentation variants during testing.
author: Hacker News

title: PopSocket phone grip with butter design sparks user enthusiasm
content:
The Verge’s Allison Johnson shares her experience adopting a phone grip, comparing the initial attraction to finding a great recipe. The story begins with a friend’s new accessory, a PopSocket-branded combo featuring a phone case with bold stripes and a grip designed to look like a stick of butter. Labeled "unsalty" and complete with tablespoon markings, the accessory was a playful nod to the current trend of butter-themed items, a fact Johnson learned from a 12-year-old friend.

Johnson describes becoming enamored with the friend’s eye-catching setup, which led her to order a similar grip for herself a few weeks later. This purchase marked a shift in her personal style, as she had previously favored buttoned-up, minimalist technology. The article details her journey from a minimalist approach to embracing a more expressive and whimsical tech accessory.
summary: A user adopted a PopSocket phone grip designed to look like a stick of butter after seeing a friend use it. The accessory features "unsalty" labeling and tablespoon markings, contrasting with the user's previous minimalist tech style.
author: The Verge

title: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
content:
Elon Musk’s America PAC spent $446 million on midterm elections, a sum the article describes as a delusional waste of nearly $500 million. The piece critiques social media’s influence, suggesting that excessive engagement with attention-seeking posts can lead to such financial missteps.

Specifically, $47 million from the PAC was directed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico. However, Talarico defeated Musk’s preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, securing 55 percent of the vote. The article notes that Talarico even made Musk’s influence a central part of his campaign.
summary: The article argues that Elon Musk delusionally threw away nearly $500 million on midterm elections. Specifically, $47 million from his America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico.
author: The Verge

title: Qualcomm targets $15B data center revenue by 2029 as smartphone sales decline
content:
Qualcomm is pivoting toward the AI data center market to offset a 20 percent decline in smartphone sales compared to 2025. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company detailed plans to expand this business segment through partnerships with Amazon and Meta, which were announced earlier in the year. Management expects this new division to grow rapidly, projecting $650 million in revenue for the first quarter of 2027.

The company forecasts that data center revenue will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029. These projections are significant relative to Qualcomm’s total revenue of $10.4 billion for 2026, highlighting the strategic importance of the data center sector to the firm’s future financial performance.
summary: Qualcomm is shifting focus to AI data centers to offset a 20 percent drop in smartphone sales. The company forecasts data center revenue will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.
author: The Verge

title: Ted Cruz pushes for Republican majority on FCC before 2027 Senate shift
content:
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) is seeking to expand the Republican majority on the Federal Communications Commission before Democrats assume control of the Senate in January 2027. Cruz announced a nomination hearing for Trump’s FCC nominee, Danielle Thumann Severs, to be held on November 10, shortly after the Republicans’ midterm loss. As the chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee for his final two months, Cruz intends to advance the Thumann Severs nomination to a full Senate vote.

Confirming Thumann Severs would establish a 3-1 Republican advantage on the FCC. This majority could shift to 3-0 by the end of 2027, as FCC Democrat Anna Gomez would be required to leave the commission at that time unless Trump agrees to renominate her.
summary: Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) is aiming to widen the Republican majority on the Federal Communications Commission before Democrats take over control of the Senate in January 2027. Just before the Republicans' midterm loss, Cruz yesterday announced a November 10 nomination hearing for Trump's FCC nominee, Danielle Thumann Severs.
author: Ars Technica

title: Elon Musk Announces SpaceX HQ Move from California to Texas Starbase
content:
Elon Musk relocated to Texas in 2020, settling outside of Austin following public disputes with California authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic. Over the subsequent six years, he intensified his commitment to the state. In 2021, Musk directed the Starship program toward South Texas, encouraging SpaceX employees to relocate for the company’s future development. That same year, in March, he began using the name Starbase to designate the production and launch facilities situated near the Rio Grande River.

Musk continued to expand SpaceX’s presence in Texas in 2023 by constructing a massive factory east of Austin. This facility is dedicated to manufacturing customer terminals and other electronics for the Starlink program. In July 2024, he announced that SpaceX would move its corporate headquarters from Hawthorne, California, to Starbase, Texas. Musk cited California’s regulatory and political environment as the primary motivation for this corporate relocation.
summary: Elon Musk moved to Texas in 2020 after disputes with California authorities and focused the Starship program and Starlink factory there. In July 2024 he announced SpaceX would relocate its corporate headquarters from Hawthorne, California to the Starbase facility in Texas, citing California's regulatory environment.
author: Ars Technica

title: Voters Pass 38 of 44 Data Center Restrictions, Slowing Trump’s AI Buildout
content: Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US. Read full article Comments
summary: In recent elections, voters approved 38 of 44 measures aimed at restricting data centers, including moratoriums and bans. The approvals slowed Trump’s AI buildout and also led to the election of officials pledging AI industry crackdowns in key states.
author: Ars Technica

title: AMD Q3 Revenue Hits $13.4B as Data Center Sales Double, Gaming Falls
content:
AMD announced third‑quarter revenues of $13.4 billion, a 45 percent increase from the same period last year. The company said its data‑center business nearly doubled, while the gaming segment declined. Chief financial officer Jean Hu noted that AMD expects revenue for the year to be roughly $17 billion, give or take 3 percent, and that the middle point of its guidance represents about 66 percent year‑over‑year growth, largely driven by the acceleration of the data‑center segment.

AMD projects fourth‑quarter revenue to rise another 27 percent from the current quarter’s results. According to Tom’s Hardware, Intel’s fourth‑quarter guidance places revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning that if both companies meet their estimates, AMD would surpass Intel’s revenue for the first time in history.

The data‑center segment grew 97 percent year over year, reaching a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes this surge to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs and the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs. In the client business, sales of AMD Ryzen mobile chips drove growth, with desktop Ryzen processors contributing $2.95 billion in revenue, up 7 percent year over year.
summary: AMD posted third‑quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45 percent year over year, with its data center segment nearly doubling and its gaming segment falling. The company’s CFO Jean Hu said the company expects total revenue of about $17 billion for the year, a 66 percent increase driven mainly by the data center business.
author: Ars Technica

title: VMware releases vSphere Express for virtualization on up to 128 cores
content:
Broadcom’s VMware has announced a new product, vSphere Express, aimed at small‑to‑medium‑sized businesses (SMBs). The offering is described as a lower‑end virtualization solution that supports up to 128 cores and is marketed as “cost‑effective essential virtualization.”

The move follows reports that many SMB customers felt pressured by VMware to adopt VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), the company’s flagship private‑cloud bundle. VCF is noted for its extensive feature set and higher cost—features that many SMBs say they do not need. In addition, some SMB users have said that VMware sales representatives previously informed them that vSphere Standard, the former entry‑level product, was no longer available. The new vSphere Express is intended to address those concerns and provide a more suitable option for smaller organizations.
summary: VMware announced vSphere Express, a lower‑end virtualization offering for organizations that require “cost‑effective essential virtualization.” The product follows reports that VMware had been pushing SMB customers toward the expensive VMware Cloud Foundation bundle and that vSphere Standard was reportedly no longer available.
author: Ars Technica

title: Uranium cubes show German nuclear program lacked sufficient material
content:
A recent study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus has clarified why the Nazi German nuclear program never produced a bomb. The paper, written by a team that included University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth, argues that the German effort lacked the necessary uranium and heavy water to build a functioning reactor, despite claims by Werner Heisenberg that they were close to criticality with the B8 pile.

Heisenberg’s 1940s project had focused on a reactor design that, according to the new research, could not reach critical mass without additional fissile material. The paper’s analysis shows that the German supply of uranium and heavy water was insufficient for the design they were pursuing, contradicting Heisenberg’s assertion that only a small amount of extra material was needed.

Koeth’s interest in the topic began in 2013 when a friend gave him a heavy‑metal cube that he immediately identified as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists. Only fourteen of these cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, Koeth and then‑graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert documented their search for the cubes’ origins, locating ten of them across the United States.

Among the cubes they found were a German uranium cube in storage at the Smithsonian Institution and another that had circulated through introductory physics courses at Harvard University. These artifacts provide tangible evidence of the German program’s attempts and help explain why the project ultimately failed.
summary: Uranium cubes show German nuclear program lacked sufficient material.
author: Ars Technica

title: Kremlin-linked hackers exploit iOS and Android flaws to infect phones via malicious sites
content:
Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws to target visitors of multiple websites, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers were assessed with “moderate to high confidence” as part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service. Their attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic profiled the device, and the final payloads, tailored to the platform, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi‑Fi passwords and full mobile device data.

The researchers noted that the attackers targeted other sites, many with links to Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, a domain belonging to a non‑partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250.holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org, delivering content from the real site that included malicious JavaScript.
summary: Kremlin-linked hackers exploit iOS and Android flaws to infect phones via malicious sites.
author: Ars Technica

title: Macronix to Stop ROM Chip Production, Impacting Nintendo Switch Cartridges
content: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM, SSDs, and GPUs. Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance. That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips. Read full article Comments
summary: Macronix announced that its ROM chip production has reached its end and it will gradually decouple from the game industry. This change may affect Nintendo, which uses Macronix as its main memory chip maker for physical Switch cartridges.
author: Ars Technica

title: Snapchat Surpasses 30 Million Paid Subscribers
content: Snapchat has surpassed 30 million paid subscribers, a milestone that follows a year after the company announced a controversial limit on free storage for its Memories feature. Users were informed that they would need to pay $1.99 per month for additional storage or subscribe to Snapchat+ to retain their Memories.

content: Following the U.S. midterm elections, President Donald Trump may encounter a turbulent final two years in office, with possible budget battles and impeachment proceedings highlighted as concerns. France 24’s International Affairs Editor Philip Turle will examine how the new political balance of power could affect his presidency.

title: Republican strategist Bryan Lanza says MAGA lost grip after midterm defeat
content:
Erin Ogunkeye recently introduced Bryan Lanza, a Republican strategist and partner in Mercury’s Washington, D.C. office, to discuss the recent midterm election. Lanza explained that the MAGA movement’s confrontational style had been a hallmark of the party, but the “veritable blue wave” that swept the election has sent a warning that the electorate wants a different approach.

Lanza noted that President Donald Trump has acknowledged the Democratic victory, sometimes adopting a combative tone and at other times a conciliatory one. He urged the president to use his remaining two years to reverse tariffs he calls damaging, address widespread dissatisfaction with immigration enforcement, and manage the highly unpopular Iran war.
summary: Following a resounding Midterm election defeat, Is MAGA Losing Its Grip on the Republican Party? Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Bryan Lanza, Republican strategist and Partner in Mercury's Washington DC office.

title: Chinese AI chatbots censor coverage of Kylian Mbappé's Mao Zedong dictator remarks
content: Footballer Kylian Mbappé sparked a wave of condemnation across China after implying that Chinese leader Mao Zedong was a dictator. According to the report, Chinese AI chatbots are censoring information about this controversy within China.
summary: Kylian Mbappé implied Chinese leader Mao Zedong was a dictator, sparking condemnation across China. Chinese AI chatbots are censoring information about the controversy.
author: France 24

title: Fact-check: Trump's second-term playbook uses fake news, AI images, and attacks critics
content:
A special fact‑checking segment hosted by Vedika Bahl examines Donald Trump’s second term, focusing on three recurring tactics. The program notes that Trump continues to launch frequent attacks on political opponents and to employ AI‑generated images that portray him favorably while advancing political narratives. It also explores the responses journalists receive when they challenge his statements.

The segment references Trump’s earlier role in popularising the phrase “fake news” and observes that his presidency has been marked by numerous false claims, conspiracy theories and misleading content.
summary: Donald Trump popularized the term “fake news” and his presidency has been filled with false claims, conspiracy theories and misleading content. Vedika Bahl’s fact‑checking segment examines his second term, noting his attacks on political opponents, use of AI‑generated images to promote himself and political narratives, and the response when journalists challenge him.
author: France 24

title: Elon Musk's $440 million Republican backing fails as candidates lose Texas races
content: Shares of Tesla and SpaceX fell after the Democratic Party won a sweeping victory in the United States midterm elections. Elon Musk, founder of both companies, contributed more than $440 million to Republican candidates and causes, making him the largest single campaign donor of the cycle. Despite that spending, the candidates he supported did not win; Musk‑backed Republicans lost the races in Texas, where he has established a personal presence.
summary: Shares of Tesla and SpaceX dropped after the Democratic party swept to power in America's midterm elections. Their founder, tech titan Elon Musk, poured over $440 million into Republican candidates and causes, the single biggest campaign donor in the election cycle.
author: France 24

title: South Africans vote in key municipal elections, testing ruling ANC
content:
Millions of South Africans are voting tonight to elect municipal governments, a result described as a crucial test for the country’s ruling African National Congress.  

Separately, Ethiopia has expelled six Sudanese diplomats, accusing Sudan of permitting the paramilitary RSF to launch drone strikes from its territory, amid a deepening humanitarian crisis that has displaced thousands following renewed fighting.
summary: Millions of South Africans are voting to elect municipal governments in a crucial test for the ruling ANC. Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese diplomats and faces a deepening humanitarian crisis as renewed fighting has displaced thousands.

title: Netanyahu alleges foreign money spent to influence Israeli parliamentary election
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday cited "serious suspicions" around foreign interference in Israel's recent parliamentary elections. He claims foreign countries spent large amounts of money to influence the results, while the largest Arab-Israeli bloc called such accusations "political persecution".
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday there are serious suspicions of foreign interference in Israel's recent parliamentary elections. He claimed foreign countries spent large amounts of money to influence the results, and the largest Arab‑Israeli bloc called the accusations political persecution.
author: France 24

title: Real Madrid win 3-2 comeback at AEK Athens with Valverde stoppage-time goal
content: Real Madrid maintained a perfect Champions League record with a 3-2 comeback win over AEK Athens on Wednesday, thanks to Federico Valverde’s 92nd‑minute long‑range strike after trailing twice. Liverpool’s opening victory streak in the competition was halted by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahçe.

title: Manchester man in 60s pleads guilty to 60+ offences after inviting men to assault wife
content: Nine men on trial in Manchester accused of either taking part in abuse or encouraging offending on internet A husband who invited other men to rape and sexually assault his wife arranged for “more and more individuals” to visit his marital home as he resolved “to satisfy his own perversity”, a jury has been told. The husband, who is in his 60s and from Stockport in Greater Manchester, has pleaded guilty to more than 60 offences against his wife. He cannot be named in order to protect the anonymity of his victim.
summary: Manchester man in 60s pleads guilty to 60+ offences after inviting men to assault wife.

title: UK government weighs restrictions on smart glasses sales amid secret filming concerns
content: Minister hints at restriction on selling technology ‘to certain users’ amid worries over surreptitious filming of women The government is considering placing restrictions on smart glasses amid concerns the technology is being used to surreptitiously film women, a minister has said. Speaking in the House of Commons, the safeguarding minister, Satvir Kaur, hinted at a ban on selling the technology “to certain users”.
summary: The UK government is considering placing restrictions on the sale of smart glasses. Safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur said the move aims to address concerns that the devices are being used to film women surreptitiously and hinted at a ban on selling them to certain users.
author: Guardian World

title: UK to begin structured dialogue with Caribbean nations on slavery reparations within a year
content: The United Kingdom has agreed to enter a “structured dialogue” within the next year with Caribbean nations that were impacted by the slave trade and its legacy, according to Commonwealth leaders. The initiative follows a consensus reported by Antigua and Barbuda’s prime minister, Gaston Browne, during the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (CHOGM). Browne said the governments present reached agreement on a way forward for slavery reparations, prompting the planned dialogue between the UK and the affected Caribbean states.
summary: The United Kingdom has agreed to a structured dialogue within the next year with Caribbean nations affected by the slave trade and its legacy, Commonwealth leaders said. Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne said the Commonwealth heads of government meeting reached a consensus on a way forward for slavery reparations.
author: Guardian World

title: Milburn review urges flexi‑jobs and subsidies for disabled youth employment
content: Exclusive: Government should introduce ‘flexi-jobs’ alongside subsidies and skills support, former minister will say The British state should create and subsidise paid jobs for thousands of disabled young people as part of an “opportunity revolution” aimed at reversing years of labour market discrimination, the Milburn review of youth employment will recommend. The review, due to report this month, will say the government should introduce “flexi-jobs” alongside employment subsidies and intensive skills support to make it easier for disabled and chronically ill 16- to 24-year-olds to get work.
summary: The Milburn review of youth employment will recommend that the government create and subsidise paid “flexi‑jobs” alongside employment subsidies and intensive skills support for disabled and chronically ill 16‑ to 24‑year‑olds. The review, due to report this month, frames the measures as an “opportunity revolution” to reverse years of labour‑market discrimination.
