title: Democrat Haley Stevens backs Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El‑Sayed
content: Endorsement was met with backlash from the party, condemning Stevens for her ‘betrayal’ Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, in an extraordinary rebuke of her party’s nominee on the eve of the midterm elections. Her endorsement came in a video posted to X after she attended an event with Rogers at the predominantly Black Perfecting church in Detroit on Sunday. Stevens’s endorsement was the culmination of an escalating feud between the former primary rivals – primarily over support for Israel – that has roiled one of the most fiercely contested Senate contests of the cycle.
summary: Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El‑Sayed, endorsed his Republican opponent Mike Rogers. The endorsement, posted in a video on X after an event at Detroit’s Perfecting church, drew backlash from Democrats who called it a betrayal.
author: Guardian World

title: All nine aboard Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, die
content: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway. Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said.
summary: All nine aboard Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, die.
author: Guardian World

title: Parents sue OpenAI after daughter dies from seizure following chatbot medication advice
content: Bowen Wan, who was taking anti‑seizure medication, received from a chatbot a schedule for tapering her dosage. After following the advice, she suffered an epileptic seizure that proved fatal. Her parents filed a lawsuit against OpenAI earlier this week, alleging that the bot’s counsel directly contributed to her death. The case adds to a series of recent lawsuits in which plaintiffs claim that advice from an artificial‑intelligence chatbot led to harmful outcomes.
summary: Bowen Wan, who was on anti‑seizure medication, received a tapering schedule from a chatbot and later died of an epileptic seizure. Her parents have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the bot’s advice caused her death.
author: Guardian World

title: Police detain up to 325 protesters outside US embassy in London over Palestine Action ban
content: Police detained a large crowd at a demonstration outside the U.S. embassy in Battersea, south London, on Saturday. Metropolitan Police initially reported 325 arrests at the protest against the proscription of the direct‑action group Palestine Action. Updated figures released on Sunday revised the total to 320 people detained for allegedly expressing support for an organisation banned under the Terrorism Act. The arrests occurred ahead of a scheduled Supreme Court hearing on Wednesday challenging the ban on Palestine Action.
summary: Police arrested 325 people on Saturday at a demonstration outside the US embassy in London against the proscription of Palestine Action. The Metropolitan Police later updated the figure to 320 detainees, saying they were held for allegedly expressing support for an organisation banned under the Terrorism Act.
author: Guardian World

title: Teen violinist Sofia Demetriades wins BBC Young Musician 2026 after first all‑female final
content: A teenage violinist, Sofia Demetriades, has been named the winner of the BBC Young Musician 2026 competition. Her victory comes after the contest’s first all‑female final in its 48‑year history. The judging panel—Joanna MacGregor, Ben Gernon and Errollyn Wallen—praised Demetriades’s rendition of Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto, describing it as “full of insights, poetry and maturity.” The award marks a notable milestone for the long‑running competition.
summary: Sofia Demetriades, a teenage violinist, won the BBC Young Musician 2026 competition in the first all‑female final in its 48‑year history. Judges Joanna MacGregor, Ben Gernon and Errollyn Wallen praised her performance of Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto as full of insights, poetry and maturity.
author: Guardian World

title: Nationals leader Matt Canavan to run for Queensland lower house seat, may face James Ashby
content:
The Nationals leader Matt Canavan has announced that he will contest a lower‑house seat in Queensland at the next federal election. His decision follows the retirement of Capricornia MP Michelle Landry, who said she will not recontest the Queensland seat.  

Canavan’s move could set up a contest with One Nation national director James Ashby, creating a potential showdown for regional seats. The announcement links the Nationals’ candidacy directly to the vacancy created by Landry’s departure.
summary: Nationals leader Matt Canavan announced he will run for a Queensland lower‑house seat at the next federal election. The announcement follows the retirement of Capricornia MP Michelle Landry and could result in a contest with One Nation national director James Ashby.
author: Guardian World

title: Natalie Nakase Leads Valkyries to WNBA Championship in 534 Days
content:
Golden State’s Golden State Valkyries captured their first WNBA title on Saturday night, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68‑63 in a Game 7 comeback that made them the fastest expansion team in major North American professional sports history to win a championship. The victory came just 534 days after the team’s inaugural game, a record that underscores the rapid rise of the franchise.

The championship roster included a point guard who had been dismissed by Dallas, a starting forward who had been waived five times, and a late‑blooming All‑Star who had been overlooked by every league team. These overlooked players found a coach who had built a career on making small openings count. Natalie Nakase, who earned a scholarship at UCLA from a walk‑on spot and secured a coaching position in Japan’s top men’s league after sending an unsolicited scouting report, brought a unique blend of trust and opportunity to the team.

Nakase’s circuitous journey taught her how to unlock potential in overlooked talent. The Valkyries’ success demonstrates the power of providing resources, responsibility, and trust to players who were once undervalued, proving the organization’s philosophy and Nakase’s leadership were key to their championship run.
summary: Natalie Nakase Leads Valkyries to WNBA Championship in 534 Days.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Premier League managers hold firm as first sacking looms after early season stability
content:
Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away.  No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season.  In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change, indicating that the early part of the campaign is often a period of stability.

The 2026‑27 season began with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026, a factor that has likely contributed to the current lack of dismissals.  The clubs have therefore been given a chance to shape their squads as they see fit without the pressure of an early change in leadership.

However, with roughly a quarter of the season already played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.  The looming break could prompt clubs to make a decision if results do not meet expectations.
summary: No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season, and all clubs began with the same manager. With roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alessia Russo scores late to earn Arsenal 1-1 draw with Aston Villa
content:
Arsenal salvaged a 1‑1 draw at home to Aston Villa when Alessia Russo scored in the 85th minute. The Gunners had dominated the match, holding almost 65 % of possession, firing 28 shots, and recording 56 touches in the opposition box compared with Villa’s four touches. The goal prevented a second straight win for the club in the league and Champions League, which had seemed to have kick‑started their season.

In the same round, Chelsea recorded a 6‑0 victory, but an England forward was taken off early during the match.
summary: Alessia Russo’s 85th‑minute goal secured a 1‑1 home draw for Arsenal against Aston Villa after the team held 65% possession. England forward James was taken off early with a hamstring injury.
author: Guardian Sport

title: 14-year-old Coventry fan turns himself in after Bradley Lowery taunt
content:
A 14-year-old Coventry City fan has surrendered himself to West Midlands police following a video posted on social media. The footage reportedly shows the boy displaying a photo of Bradley Lowery while taunting Sunderland supporters during the clubs’ Premier League match on Saturday.

Bradley Lowery, a Sunderland fan, gained widespread attention after being diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He passed away in 2017 at the age of six.
summary: A 14-year-old boy handed himself in to West Midlands police after a video showed a Coventry fan displaying a photo of Bradley Lowery during a Sunderland match. Bradley Lowery died at age six in 2017 from neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Borthwick urges England to improve discipline ahead of Nations Championship
content: ‘A big breakdown challenge is coming,’ warns head coach Genge calls timing of ‘hip-drop’ tackle law change ‘beserk’ Steve Borthwick is urging his England players to act smarter and recognise the vital importance of keeping 15 players on the field before a pivotal month for the national team. Borthwick’s side have been shown 14 yellow cards and one red in 2026 to date and, partly as a consequence, have lost five of their past seven Tests. Borthwick is also concerned that different refereeing interpretations in the domestic Prem are not helping England at international level, with the latest complication being a mid‑season law change preventing so-called “hip-drop” tackles. His experienced prop Ellis Genge has called the timing of the alteration “berserk” but also fully accepts England must improve their disciplinary record in their autumn Nations Championship fixtures.
summary: Steve Borthwick has warned England players to act smarter and keep all 15 players on the field before the Nations Championship. England has received 14 yellow cards and one red in 2026, lost five of its last seven Tests, and must improve its disciplinary record amid a new 'hip‑drop' tackle law change.
author: Guardian Sport

In the Vikings-Lions game, Detroit leads 9-0 in the first quarter after punting following sacks by Andrew van Ginkel and Eric Wilson. Minnesota took possession from their 10-yard line, while Buffalo’s J. Allen recorded a one-yard rush.

title: Arsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces early
content:
Arsenal secured their first league victory at Liverpool since September 2012, a win highlighted by an early goal from Kai Havertz. The article describes the match as a display of the team’s ruthless approach and the champion knowhow they developed during last season. As Arsenal returned to London, the piece notes that they made a statement, asserting that they remain the Premier League’s team to beat, regardless of the outcome of Manchester City’s financial rule breaches.

Mikel Arteta was part of the Arsenal midfield during the club’s previous league win at Anfield in September 2012. However, the manager’s memories of that specific match are described as hazy due to a concussion he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.
summary: It was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they accumulated over the course of last season. As they headed back to London, they did so having made a statement.

title: Conifers in Southern Hemisphere Grow Four Times Faster, More Drought-Resistant
content: A study covering 192 sites across four continents found that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster and exhibit greater drought resistance than those in their native ranges. These findings highlight how some trees thrive far from home, with implications for the effectiveness of carbon sinks.
summary: Researchers studied 192 sites across four continents and found that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster than those in their native ranges. The Southern Hemisphere conifers also show greater drought resistance.
author: Phys.org

title: Mediterranean Climate Not Tropical Despite Warmer Seas and Shifting Pressures
content: Nowhere in the Iberian Peninsula or the Balearic Islands has a tropical climate—for this to be the case, the average temperature in the coldest month would have to be 18°C (64 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.
summary: The Iberian Peninsula and Balearic Islands do not have a tropical climate because the average temperature in the coldest month is below 18°C. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers and the low winter temperatures do not match tropical climate patterns.
author: Phys.org

content: Tino Marolo and his dog Stella search in the dark woods of Piedmont, guided by a flashlight, for one of Italy’s most prized culinary treasures hidden beneath the soil. The hunt underscores a growing concern: a warming climate threatens these prized white truffles from Italy to Croatia.
summary: Guided by the beam of a flashlight, Tino Marolo follows his dog Stella through the darkness of a Piedmont woodland, searching for one of Italy's most prized culinary treasures hidden beneath the soil.

title: Perseverance uses spacesuit swatches to test if Martian dust is less abrasive than lunar dust
content: NASA’s Perseverance rover carries tiny swatches of spacesuit material—each less than a square inch (6.5 cm²)—among its sensors, cameras and navigation tools. The swatches are used to evaluate the potential damage caused by Martian dust. According to the title, these samples suggest that Mars dust may be less abrasive than lunar dust.
summary: NASA's Mars rover Perseverance is wearing small swatches of spacesuit material. The swatches, each less than a square inch in size, are helping scientists assess whether Martian dust is less abrasive than lunar dust.

title: Fiona Walker's report reveals Covid deaths 4-6x higher for UK learning disability patients
content: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker. “I know from experience they wouldn’t have valued my life,” she says, in a new report on the treatment of people with learning disabilities during the crisis. The 1.5 million people in the UK with learning disabilities, and their families, had reason for concern. Death rates in England were four to six times higher than average for people with learning disabilities. As is now well established, the pandemic did not create inequalities; it exposed and intensified them. People with learning disabilities die on average 19.5 years earlier than people without, and deaths are almost twice as likely to be classed as avoidable.
summary: The Covid pandemic shed an unforgiving light on health and social care inequalities. The lessons have yet to be absorbed The fear that so many felt as the death toll rose during the Covid pandemic was magnified for Fiona Walker.
author: Guardian Science

title: Show HN: HackerBooks aggregates 16.5k books mentioned on Hacker News
content:
A developer has launched HackerBooks, a website designed to track books mentioned on Hacker News, inspired by Karpathy’s HackerTube. The site catalogues approximately 16,500 books that at least two distinct HN commenters have referenced between 2007 and the present. Each entry links back to the specific comments where the book was mentioned, and the underlying data is available for download from the site’s about page.

The creator states that Claude Opus 5.5 wrote almost all of the project, including the data pipeline and the website itself, while the developer handled steering, decision-making, and purchasing the domain. The tool counts all mentions, meaning both praise and criticism contribute to a book’s tally. The project has garnered 511 points and 130 comments on Hacker News, with the creator inviting users to report missing titles or incorrect matches.
summary: HackerBooks, created with Claude’s assistance, lists about 16.5 k books that at least two Hacker News commenters have mentioned since 2007, with each book linking back to the comments. The author steered the project, purchased the domain, and provides downloadable data from the site’s about page.
author: Hacker News

title: Ask HN: Users seek privacy‑focused TVs for Apple TV use, 60‑80″ 4K display
content:

They are willing to pay a premium and have heard that Apple TV offers better privacy than many native smart‑TV apps. The user asks whether certain TVs pair better with Apple TV for privacy and wants to know what success others have had.

The post includes a link to the discussion thread on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50328896). The thread has 17 points and 19 comments, indicating some community engagement around the topic.
summary: A Hacker News user asked for recommendations for a privacy‑respecting TV sized 60‑80 inches with 4K resolution and at least 60 Hz, willing to pay a premium. The user prefers using Apple TV as the sole smart platform and asked which TVs pair best for privacy, receiving 17 points and 19 comments.

title: Dying star 1,600 ly away shows two dust rings from former planets
content:
Astronomers have identified a dying star 1,600 light‑years from Earth that is surrounded by two rings of gas and dust.  

The rings are thought to be remnants of planetary bodies that the star once hosted.
summary: A dying star 1,600 light-years from Earth is surrounded by two rings of gas and dust. Astronomers believe the rings are remnants of the planetary bodies the star once hosted.

title: Playable version of canceled Portal prequel F‑Stop leaked
content:
Leakers have assembled a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F‑Stop. Most of the assets for the build came from the massive 12‑terabyte leak that dropped in August; the leak did not include the game’s source code or map data.  

Those missing pieces apparently surfaced on the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together.  

Some dialog and elements from F‑Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2. The prequel differs from the mainline Portal games by centering on a camera mechanic that lets players capture an item by taking its picture and then place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid.
summary: Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop. Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August.

title: Apple’s HomeView may gain security camera mode with HomeKit Secure Video
content:
Reddit user pdfu has uncovered clues in the HomeView 27.2 firmware that suggest Apple may be adding security‑camera functionality to its smart‑home hub. The firmware strings reference a “security camera mode” that includes motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, along with privacy features.

A setup page in the code explicitly states: “Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video.” According to pdfu, the camera feeds would be viewable only by members of the home and would display an indicator light and emit a sound when the feed is being watched or when recording begins. The analysis stops short of detailing further privacy measures.
summary: Reddit user pdfu found hints hidden in the HomeView 27.2 code that Apple could be adding security camera features to its smart home hub. The strings describe a security camera mode with motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, as well as privacy functions.

title: Police Chief Eric Fadden disconnects Flock cameras after council fails to respond
content:
More municipalities are ending contracts with surveillance firm Flock Safety, but several are encountering obstacles. In Plymouth, Minnesota, the city council voted in September to terminate its agreement with Flock, yet the company did not respond to the city’s cancellation request. The cameras stayed operational for more than a month without acknowledgment from Flock.

Consequently, Police Chief Eric Fadden ordered staff to unplug the devices. He said that after receiving no reply for over a week, he directed the power cords be disconnected to ensure the cameras were no longer functioning.
summary: Police Chief Eric Fadden disconnects Flock cameras after council fails to respond.
author: The Verge

title: Charisma as a Red Flag: How a Bar Conversation Revealed Manipulation
content: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired. We discussed topics I know little about: the instability of modern economies, the feasibility of commercial space travel, the likelihood of a coup in Russia. I found myself leaning in and asking questions: I felt as if I could learn a lot from this person. We eventually got to psychology, which is more my wheelhouse. I brooded about how easy it’s become for people to accept strange ideas. “Some people will believe anything,” he observed. “Some people even believe the Earth is round!” It’s increasingly difficult to ignore how fragmented and bizarre our beliefs have become. We live in our own echo chambers, defined by the channels, feeds and influencers we follow. As a result we can arrive at very polarised conclusions about vaccines, the climate, gender, geopolitics, the shape of the Earth and everything else. Disagreements on topics like these frequently damage relationships, alienate friends and estrange loved ones.
summary: The narrator recounts a conversation with a charismatic stranger in a bar who discussed topics the narrator knew little about, including economics, space travel, and geopolitics. The narrator reflects that charisma can lead people to accept bizarre ideas, contributing to polarized beliefs that damage relationships.
author: Guardian Technology

title: 2026 Youth Olympic Games open in Dakar, first Olympic event in Africa
content: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games have officially kicked off in Senegal. Crowds gathered for Saturday's opening ceremony, featuring hundreds of drummers and dancers celebrating Senegalese and wider African culture, in keeping with the Games' motto: “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”. It is the first-ever Olympic sporting event to be held on the African continent, but comes as Senegal faces an economic crisis. The country's president has said he wants to turn sport into an “economic and social engine”. The Games also come amid a government crackdown on LGBTQ+ people. Nearly 3,000 teenagers from more than 200 countries are competing in around a dozen sports, including athletics, beach wrestling and a five-a-side version of baseball. Jean-Loup Chappelet, Professor at Lausanne University and Olympics specialist, shares further insights.
summary: 2026 Youth Olympic Games open in Dakar, first Olympic event in Africa.
author: France 24

title: Senegal hosts first Youth Olympic Games in Africa
content:
Senegal hosts the first Olympic event on the African continent. The Youth Olympics marked the first African Games in over 130 years, opening ceremony led by Senegal’s president in Dakar.  

A total of 136 Senegalese athletes are competing, with the event supported by 6,000 local volunteers.
summary: The Youth Olympic Games opened in Dakar, marking the first Olympic event held on the African continent in over 130 years and were inaugurated by Senegal’s president. The games feature 136 Senegalese athletes and are supported by 6,000 local volunteers.

title: Kherson ceasefire ends Sunday after Russia declines extension
content: The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, confined to the Kherson region, was scheduled to end on Sunday evening after Russia declined to extend it. The pause, which began on Tuesday, had allowed a humanitarian mission to the Russian‑occupied town of Olechky.
summary: The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, localized in Kherson, was set to end on Sunday evening after Russia refused to extend it. The pause, which began on Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian‑occupied town of Olechky.

title: France sees third weekend of protests over living costs, education, largely peaceful
content: France experienced its third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, drawing more than 320,000 participants. While most demonstrations remained peaceful, police deployed tear gas to disperse clashes, and authorities recorded over 770 arrests nationwide. France24 journalist Jamie Smith‑Maillet provided additional commentary.
summary: More than 320,000 people protested across France for the third consecutive weekend over living costs and education, and most demonstrations remained peaceful. Police used tear gas in some clashes and authorities reported more than 770 arrests nationwide.

title: Evacuations from Oleshky end during first humanitarian truce
content:
Residents of Oleshky who had asked to leave were reunited with their families in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31, concluding the evacuations carried out during the first humanitarian truce of the war.  

The city, situated on the front line and under Russian occupation, remains in a humanitarian crisis, with civilians lacking even basic necessities. A localized ceasefire has been in place since Tuesday, as reported by France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze.
summary: Residents of Oleshky who had requested evacuation were reunited with their loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31. The front‑line city under Russian occupation, facing a humanitarian crisis, has been under a localised ceasefire since Tuesday, the first humanitarian truce of the war.

content: Thousands joined an opposition protest in New Delhi on Sunday, where India’s opposition parties demonstrated against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and a nationwide voter‑list review that has sparked demonstrations since the summer. The rally was led by the youth movement Cockroach Janta Party, according to reporter Eliza Herbert.

content:
The solo transatlantic Route du Rhum race launched from Saint‑Malo on Sunday with 115 sailors setting off in mild weather. The fleet left at 12:02 GMT, heading along the Brittany coast in light winds toward a mandatory checkpoint near Cap Fréhel, where spectators had gathered.

Competitor Nicolas d’Estais called the conditions “ideal” before boarding his yacht Café Joyeux. The departure was reported from Saint‑Malo by Selina Sykes.

National Grid has taken a step toward building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, a facility that could supply power to a large neighboring datacentre as the UK expands its AI infrastructure.

content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is set to announce new immigration rules on Monday that will extend the waiting period for legal migrants to obtain indefinite leave to remain in the UK. Under the proposals, most migrants would have to wait about ten years, while some could face up to fifteen years before qualifying for settlement.

MPs have warned that the measures could trigger staff shortages in health and social‑care sectors and risk a second Windrush‑type scandal. Ministers, including Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, have expressed concern that care workers already in the country may be subject to the longest, fifteen‑year, waiting period.
summary: Shabana Mahmood will announce new rules on Monday that require most legal migrants to wait about a decade and some up to 15 years for indefinite leave to remain. MPs and ministers, including housing secretary Angela Rayner, warned the measures could worsen staff shortages in health and social care.

content:
Indirect talks in Doha entered their third day on Sunday, with Qatar working to secure the release of more than $6 billion in Iranian assets. The effort is aimed at opening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

Officials from Gulf states say they are “braced for the worst” as they await Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait before the U.S. mid‑term elections on Tuesday. The outcome of the talks could determine whether the waterway resumes operation and whether nuclear talks resume.
summary: Gulf officials ‘braced for worst’ as Qatar seeks $6bn asset release to reopen Hormuz.

content:
French officials have opened an investigation into the attempted murder of a police officer after a petrol bomb was thrown at riot police during youth‑led protests that spread to cities across France, Germany, Switzerland, Portugal and Albania.  

Germany’s interior minister has called for harsh penalties in response to the violence. In Portugal, police – some accompanied by dogs – cleared protest camps with baton charges, while security forces in Switzerland were attacked with paving stones.

title: UK ready to spend £450m annually on EU students if granted Made in Europe access
content:
Ministers have indicated that the UK is willing to spend up to £450 million a year to allow students from the European Union to pay the same university fees as British students. The proposal, described as an exclusive plan, would involve compensating universities for the discounted rates.

The UK government has drawn up the framework for the fee parity, according to sources. It would enable EU students arriving from the continent to pay identical fees to those paid by domestic students.

The proposal is contingent on the UK gaining access to the European Union’s “Made in Europe” industrial programme, Brussels’ approval of which is a prerequisite for the fee‑equalisation plan.
summary: Ministers are prepared to spend up to £450 million a year to give EU students discounted university fees, the Guardian reports. The funding is conditional on Brussels allowing the UK to join the EU's Made in Europe industrial programme.

title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, hitting Kstovo and Samara sites
content:
Ukraine has resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries despite pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, and the Kremlin says Kyiv is “simply ignoring” U.S. wishes. The renewed strikes come as a cease‑fire in the occupied town of Oleshky is set to end late on Sunday.  

Russian state media reported that Ukrainian long‑range drones set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, shortly after a major strike on another large refinery in Samara oblast that is owned by the state energy giant Rosneft.
summary: Ukraine has resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries, defying pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections. Russian state media reported Ukrainian long-range drones set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast and struck a major Rosneft‑owned refinery in Samara oblast.

title: UK agrees to reparations dialogue but keeps slavery issue off CHOGM agenda
content:
British prime minister Boris Johnson has agreed to enter a structured dialogue on reparatory justice, though the issue will not appear on the formal agenda of the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. British officials initially insisted that discussions of slavery reparations should be excluded from the summit and warned that Labour mayor Andy Burnham would refuse to attend if the topic were formally included, a Caribbean political figure said.

Ralph Gonsalves, former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the Repair Campaign reparatory‑justice movement, welcomed Britain’s decision to engage in dialogue but said the United Kingdom had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
summary: UK agrees to reparations dialogue but keeps slavery issue off CHOGM agenda.

content: Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, is expected to appear in court again while she awaits a ruling on whether her case will be retried. The upcoming hearing will determine the next steps in the prosecution.
summary: Lindsay Clancy, a Massachusetts mother, is accused of murdering her three children. She is expected back in court as she awaits a decision on whether her case will be retried.

title: Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 Spacecraft Toward Mars on Nov. 1, 1962
content:
On November 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft, marking the country’s fourth attempt to send a probe to the Red Planet. The launch was part of the broader Space Race, and the mission’s objective was a fly‑by of Mars.

Immediately after separating from its launch vehicle, Mars 1 deployed its solar panels and entered a cruise phase toward Mars. Mission controllers received telemetry that revealed a leak in one of the gas valves that controlled the spacecraft’s orientation system. With the orientation system compromised, the probe could not reliably point its antennas toward Earth, and contact was lost when the spacecraft was roughly halfway to Mars.

Despite the loss of communication, Mars 1 did reach Mars and performed a fly‑by, providing the first close‑approach data about the planet. The mission was the Soviet Union’s first to get near enough to reveal early details about Mars, although it was not considered a complete success due to the orientation failure and loss of contact.

Mars 1’s launch followed three earlier Soviet attempts that ended in launch failures. Two years later, NASA’s Mariner IV became the first successful fly‑by mission to Mars. The 1962 Soviet mission remains a notable milestone in early interplanetary exploration.

For additional space‑history content, the “On This Day In Space” archive and related videos are available on YouTube.
summary: The Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on Nov. 1, 1962, to fly by Mars. It lost contact with Earth about halfway to the planet after a gas valve leak caused a loss of orientation.

title: Young Vic to livestream Milo Rau’s documentary play on Gisèle Pelicot trial on Nov 30
content:
The Young Vic’s upcoming production of Milo Rau’s four‑hour documentary play about the trial of the men who drugged and raped Gisèle Pelicot is set to run at London’s County Hall on 30 November. The show, created with Servane Dècle, has already been performed worldwide and sold out quickly. It will be livestreamed in full, offering audiences a chance to experience the piece from home.

Rau, a Swiss director known for his “ripped‑from‑the‑headlines” approach, has previously staged works on wars in Iraq and Congo and on the exploitation of migrant workers. His new play focuses on the factual details of the trial rather than conventional theatrical set pieces, a point highlighted by Young Vic boss Nadia Fall.

The cast features Adjoa Andoh, Rosie Jones and Olivia Williams. Fall remarked that the act of witnessing the facts “really got me” and that the production “just floors you.”
summary: The four‑hour documentary play about the trial of the men who drugged and raped Gisèle Pelicot, created by Milo Rau with Servane Dècle, will be staged by the Young Vic at London’s County Hall on 30 November. The sold‑out production, starring Adjoa Andoh, Rosie Jones and Olivia Williams, will be livestreamed in full.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Ariarne Titmus discusses retirement, health, and intense former coach
content: The Australian swimming great on her decision to retire, her health and fertility journey – and her ‘intense’ former coach From a life tracing the black line three metres below the water’s surface, to one marked by shades of grey, Ariarne Titmus is still adapting. Now 26, and two years removed from her final competitive event, she recognises her excellence as a swimmer only partly prepared her for what came next. “I look at a lot of things in my life pretty black and white, which is probably not a good way to be sometimes,” she says. “In my swimming career, I was all or nothing. I was win or lose. I was achieve it, or fail. And I guess that’s not a great way to be in life.”
summary: Australian swimmer Ariarne Titmus reflects on her retirement, health, and fertility journey. She acknowledges that her previous all-or-nothing competitive mindset was not ideal for life outside of swimming.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Harriet Dart wins maiden WTA title at 30 in Guangzhou Open
content:
Britain’s Harriet Dart claimed her maiden WTA title at the Guangzhou Open in China by defeating 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger with a score of 4-6, 6-3, 6-4. The 30-year-old qualifier, ranked as the British No 5, came from a set down to secure the victory in what was her first WTA final.

Dart’s path to the final included a semi-final win over Sun Xinran, during which she saved three match points. In the final match against the fourth seed, Dart dropped her serve in the opening game and faced a break point in her subsequent service game before establishing a foothold. Although she broke back to reach 4-4, Tagger, who won the 2025 junior French Open, responded to take the first set.
summary: Briton Harriet Dart, 30, won her first WTA title at the Guangzhou Open after defeating 18‑year‑old Lilli Tagger 4‑6, 6‑3, 6‑4. The qualifier saved three match points in her semi‑final win over Sun Xinran and is ranked British No 5.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Michael Carrick remains Manchester United manager for Roma match
content:
Michael Carrick is expected to remain in charge of Manchester United for Tuesday’s Champions League match against Roma at Old Trafford, despite the team’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. The loss has left United in 17th place in the Premier League, marking their first win in nine games and their poorest start to a season since 1988.

No managerial change is anticipated until the international break. Carrick’s position is set to be reviewed again after the next round of Premier League fixtures, during which United will host Aston Villa next Sunday.
summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford. The decision comes after a 2‑0 loss to Chelsea and will be reviewed again during the international break.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34
content:
Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34, her family announced. The athlete, who is from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, passed away at 6.30am on Sunday. Mageean was a two-time Olympic competitor who secured the European 1500m title in Rome in 2024.

In a social media post, her family stated that she was surrounded by her loved ones at the time of her death. They described her as a “beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many,” noting that she will be deeply missed.
summary: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
content:
Manchester City defeated London City Lionesses at Bromley, securing a three-point victory in a thrilling encounter. Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp scored for the visitors, with Hemp restoring City’s lead after Jana Fernández equalized for the home side. The result extended the gap between the two teams to six points.

The loss dealt a blow to London City Lionesses’ title ambitions, though their performance remains impressive in only their second Women’s Super League season. Despite the defeat, the home team delivered a statement performance that kept them in the conversation as contenders for this season’s title.
summary: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller.

content: Some Democrats criticize Iowa Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek for a recent ad on transgender sports and gender‑affirming care. Turek, a Paralympian who grew up in a wheelchair, says he believes no Iowan should face discrimination and that rules are important.

content: A federal judge on Saturday dismissed President Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal for the second time. The president had originally filed the suit last year after the newspaper published details of a 2003 letter he allegedly sent.

content:
